library(mvgam)

Monitoring programmes often measure one quantity with several methods.
A population might be counted along transects, weighed in traps and
detected by cameras in the same months. Each method measures the same
abundance through an observation process of its own. Fitted
separately, each method estimates abundance from its own data alone.
Fitted jointly, every method informs one estimate of the shared
abundance. Integrated population models combine data sources in this
way (Schaub and Abadi
[2011](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10336-010-0632-7)).

mvgam fits such a model as a multivariate formula: one `bf()` per
response, each with its own family and covariates. A single
`trend_formula` describes the latent process they share. This article
simulates three methods observing one population. We fit the joint
model and the three separate models, then compare how closely each
recovers the simulated abundance.

## The data

The latent abundance $z_t$, on the log scale, follows a stationary
AR(1) over 80 months:

$$
z_t \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0.7\, z_{t-1},\ 0.4).
$$

Three methods observe it. Transect counts (`count`) are Poisson with a
log link. Survey effort varies by month and enters as an offset. Trap
biomass (`biomass`) is Gamma with a log link and shape 2. A seasonal
cycle in month adds to the latent state. Camera detections (`camera`)
are Bernoulli with a logit link. Detection rises by 0.05 on the logit
scale with each day the camera is deployed. The cameras run in only 60
of the 80 months.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(2024)
n_time <- 80
z <- numeric(n_time)
z[1] <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.4 / sqrt(1 - 0.7^2))
for (t in 2:n_time) {
  z[t] <- 0.7 * z[t - 1] + rnorm(1, 0, 0.4)
}

month <- (seq_len(n_time) - 1) %% 12 + 1
log_effort <- log(runif(n_time, 0.8, 1.2))
deploy_days <- runif(n_time, 5, 20)
mu_biomass <- exp(0.5 + sin(2 * pi * month / 12) + z)

mv_data <- data.frame(
  time = seq_len(n_time),
  series = factor("pop1"),
  month = month,
  log_effort = log_effort,
  deploy_days = deploy_days,
  count = rpois(n_time, exp(1.5 + log_effort + z)),
  biomass = rgamma(n_time, shape = 2, rate = 2 / mu_biomass),
  camera = rbinom(n_time, 1, plogis(-0.5 + 0.05 * deploy_days + z))
)
mv_data$camera[-sort(sample.int(n_time, 60))] <- NA
```

```{r plot-data, fig.asp = 0.8, fig.cap = "The three simulated monitoring records. The camera record has gaps in the months the cameras did not run."}
observed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("count", "biomass", "camera"), function(r) {
  data.frame(time = mv_data$time, value = mv_data[[r]], response = r)
}))
observed$response <- factor(observed$response,
                            levels = c("count", "biomass", "camera"))
ggplot(observed, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line(data = ~ subset(.x, response != "camera"), colour = "#A25050") +
  geom_point(size = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ response, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Month", y = NULL)
```

## The joint model

Each response enters through its own `bf()`, combined with `+`,
carrying its family and its covariates. `set_rescor(FALSE)` declares that the responses
share no residual correlation beyond the latent state. A cyclic smooth
of month captures the seasonal cycle in biomass:

```{r joint-fit}
joint_formula <-
  bf(count ~ 1 + offset(log_effort), family = poisson()) +
  bf(biomass ~ 1 + s(month, bs = "cc", k = 8), family = Gamma(link = "log")) +
  bf(camera ~ 1 + deploy_days, family = bernoulli()) +
  set_rescor(FALSE)

mod_joint <- mvgam(
  joint_formula,
  trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
  data = mv_data,
  knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
  chains = 4, seed = 2024, silent = 2
)
```

The latent state $z_t$ enters the linear predictor of every response.
Because a response with no record drops out of the likelihood, a month
without a camera record informs the state through the count and
biomass likelihoods alone.

## Checking each response

`pp_check()` compares draws from the posterior predictive distribution
with the data. Without `resp` it draws one panel per response:

```{r ppc, fig.asp = 1, fig.cap = "Posterior predictive checks for each response. A rootogram compares the frequency of each count. A density overlay checks the biomass record. Bars give the share of each camera outcome."}
pp_check(mod_joint, ndraws = 50)
```

`conditional_effects()` draws each response's covariate effects on
that response's scale, with the latent process held out. The
simulated biomass cycle peaks in month 3:

```{r effects, fig.asp = 0.45, fig.width = 8, fig.cap = "Expected biomass by month and camera detection probability by deployment days, with 95% credible intervals."}
ce <- conditional_effects(mod_joint)
wrap_plots(plot(ce, plot = FALSE), ncol = 2)
```

```{r slope-numbers, include = FALSE}
slope <- as.numeric(as_draws_matrix(
  mod_joint, variable = "b_camera_deploy_days"
))
fe_slope <- sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", mean(slope),
                    quantile(slope, 0.025), quantile(slope, 0.975))
bm <- ce[["biomass"]][["month"]]$data
bm_peak <- round(bm$month[which.max(bm$estimate)])
```

The fitted biomass curve peaks in month `r bm_peak`. The deployment
slope is `r fe_slope` on the logit scale, against the 0.05 used to
simulate the data.

## What the joint model gains

To compare, we fit each method on its own, with the same AR(1) state:

```{r separate-fits}
fit_one <- function(formula, family) {
  mvgam(formula, trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1), family = family,
        data = mv_data, knots = list(month = c(0.5, 12.5)),
        chains = 4, seed = 2024, silent = 2)
}
mod_count <- fit_one(count ~ 1 + offset(log_effort), poisson())
mod_biomass <- fit_one(biomass ~ 1 + s(month, bs = "cc", k = 8),
                       Gamma(link = "log"))
mod_camera <- fit_one(camera ~ 1 + deploy_days, bernoulli())
```

`hindcast(type = "trend")` returns each model's posterior for the
latent state:

```{r recovery-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.asp = 0.62, out.width = "95%", fig.cap = "Posterior medians and 95% credible intervals of the latent state from the joint model and from each method alone. Crosses mark the simulated state."}
fits <- list(
  "Joint" = mod_joint,
  "Counts alone" = mod_count,
  "Biomass alone" = mod_biomass,
  "Camera alone" = mod_camera
)
truth <- data.frame(time = seq_len(n_time), z = z)
wrap_plots(lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {
  plot(hindcast(fits[[nm]], type = "trend")) +
    geom_point(aes(time, z), data = truth, shape = 4, size = 1) +
    labs(title = nm, y = "Latent state")
}), ncol = 2)
```

```{r recovery-table}
recovery <- t(vapply(fits, function(fit) {
  s <- summary(hindcast(fit, type = "trend"))
  c(RMSE = sqrt(mean((s$predQ50 - z)^2)),
    `Interval width` = mean(s$predQ97.5 - s$predQ2.5))
}, numeric(2)))
round(recovery, 2)
```

```{r recovery-numbers, include = FALSE}
by_rmse <- rownames(recovery)[order(recovery[, "RMSE"])]
fe_ranking <- knitr::combine_words(paste0(
  tolower(by_rmse), " (", sprintf("%.2f", recovery[by_rmse, "RMSE"]), ")"
))
narrowest <- tolower(rownames(recovery)[
  which.min(recovery[, "Interval width"])
])
widest <- tolower(rownames(recovery)[
  which.max(recovery[, "Interval width"])
])
```

Ordered by root mean squared error against the simulated state, the
fits rank `r fe_ranking`. Intervals are narrowest in the `r narrowest`
fit and widest in the `r widest` fit. A single binary record per month
constrains abundance weakly.

## Forecasts

`forecast()` extends the latent state past the last month and passes
it through each response's observation model. The new data hold unit
survey effort, the calendar month of each future time point and 15
deployment days for the camera. `type = "expected"` returns the
expected count, the expected biomass and the detection probability:

```{r forecast, fig.asp = 1, fig.cap = "Expected values for each response over the training months and a six-month forecast. Points are the observations."}
newdata <- data.frame(
  time = n_time + 1:6,
  series = factor("pop1"),
  month = (n_time + 0:5) %% 12 + 1,
  log_effort = 0,
  deploy_days = 15,
  count = NA, biomass = NA, camera = NA
)
fc <- forecast(mod_joint, newdata = newdata, type = "expected")
plot(fc)
```

The forecast object also feeds `score()` once the held-out
observations arrive.

Against the simulated abundance, the four fits ranked `r fe_ranking`
by error. A single binary outcome per month constrains the state
weakly. Fitted jointly, the camera record takes the state the other
methods estimate. A monitoring programme that measures one population by several methods
can fit them to one latent process and let each method inform the
rest.
